headline: Bohm's walk-off single in 10th beats Mets, 5-4
recap: The Phillies and Mets went to extra innings tied 4-4 after Brett Baty's solo homer off Craig Kimbrel erased a Philadelphia lead in the top of the ninth. In the bottom of the 10th, Trea Turner opened the frame on second base as the automatic extra-innings runner. The Mets intentionally walked Bryce Harper to set up a force, but Alec Bohm lined a single to right off Adam Ottavino that scored Turner without a throw, ending it 5-4 with none out.

Taijuan Walker started for the Phillies and worked six innings, allowing two runs on five hits with a walk and four strikeouts. Mets starter Tylor Megill matched him for length, giving up three runs on five hits over six innings with a walk and six strikeouts.

J.T. Realmuto's three-run homer in the sixth, his 20th of the season, put Philadelphia ahead after Bryce Harper was hit by a pitch and Bohm singled ahead of him. Seranthony Dominguez worked a scoreless top of the 10th, walking two and striking out two, to pick up the win after Kimbrel was charged with his fourth blown save.
